Package neqsim.process.fielddevelopment.olga

Class OlgaWellGenkeyExporter

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.fielddevelopment.olga.OlgaWellGenkeyExporter
public final class OlgaWellGenkeyExporter extends Object
Exports a well's liquid inflow performance relationship and trajectory as OLGA GENKEY text: case-level MATERIAL/WALL/TABULAR library keywords followed by a NETWORKCOMPONENT TYPE=FLOWPATH well network-component block, ready to embed inside a full genkey case.

This bridges two already-validated NeqSim pieces -- InflowPerformance (the liquid IPR model) and an externally supplied trajectory (node coordinates and per-segment diameters, e.g. from a real deviation survey or a synthetic trajectory generator) -- into the real OLGA keyword syntax the Petroleum Experts/Schlumberger OLGA engine reads: MATERIAL, WALL, a TABULAR inflow-performance table, GEOMETRY, PIPE segments, HEATTRANSFER, and RESERVOIRCONTACT.

Validated against a real OLGA rule-check

This class's exact output was embedded in a full genkey case (adapted from the olga-genkey skill's own Basic.genkey reference case) and run through the real, installed OLGA engine's -exitRC rule check repeatedly, not just inspected by eye. That process caught several real structural bugs no unit test alone found (unit tests only assert substring presence, not validity within OLGA's own keyword hierarchy):

  • TABULAR and WALL nested inside the FLOWPATH instead of at case level ("Unknown keyword type ... for FLOWPATH").
  • POSITION LABEL=Bottomhole referencing the wrong (last, not first) pipe.
  • GEOMETRY and HEATTRANSFER entirely missing ("Missing required keywords").
  • A bare WALL ... MATERIAL=(STEEL) reference with no matching MATERIAL declaration ("MATERIAL with LABEL or NUMBER STEEL ... is not found") -- OLGA has no built-in material by that name.

All are fixed and covered by regression tests; see OlgaWellGenkeyExporterTest for the specifics.

Trajectory convention

xMetre/yMetre are per-NODE coordinates (meters, OLGA's own elevation convention: yMetre negative with depth), starting at the well's own origin (index 0, the deepest/reservoir-contact end). diameterMetre is per-SEGMENT, so it has exactly one fewer entry than xMetre/yMetre -- segment i (1-indexed PIPE i) runs from node i-1 to node i with diameter diameterMetre[i-1].

Deliberately out of scope

This class exports only what its real inputs actually determine. It does not fabricate a placeholder for data it has no way to know:

  • No choke valve / Cv table. A well-specific choke restriction is not implied by an IPR or a trajectory; a non-well-specific placeholder Cv table would misrepresent an actual choke restriction. Add a choke to the embedding case separately once real Cv data is available.
  • No segment grading. Each consecutive node pair becomes exactly one PIPE with NSEGMENT=1. Provide more trajectory nodes for finer resolution; this class does not invent a grading heuristic.
  • No fabricated GOR/WGR. InflowPerformance models stock-tank liquid rate only and carries no gas-oil or water-gas ratio. GORST=/WGR= are omitted from RESERVOIRCONTACT unless supplied explicitly (they are optional overrides in OLGA's own genkey format; omitting them defers to the fluid file's own composition).
  • No assumed material properties. setWall(double, String, String, double, double, double) requires a real conductivity/heat-capacity/density, not just a material name -- an earlier version of this class accepted a bare name like "STEEL" and rule-checked as invalid because OLGA has no built-in material by that name.

Example usage


 InflowPerformance ipr = InflowPerformance.composite(200.0, 70.68, 66.94);
 OlgaWellGenkeyExporter exporter = new OlgaWellGenkeyExporter("WELL-1");
 exporter.setTrajectory(new double[] {0.0, 0.0, 0.0}, new double[] {0.0, -1000.0, -2000.0},
     new double[] {0.1500, 0.1240});
 exporter.setInflowPerformance(ipr);
 exporter.setReservoirTemperature(90.0, "C");
 exporter.setPipeRoughness(2.0e-5, "m"); // real tubing roughness, not a guess
 exporter.setWall(0.012, "m", "CARBON_STEEL", 50.0, 500.0, 7850.0); // real material properties, not a guess
 exporter.setHeatTransfer(6.5, "W/m2-C", 6.0, "C"); // real ambient U-value/temperature, not a guess
 exporter.setPvtFluidLabel("MY_FLUID"); // the FLUID= label a PVT table generator already produced
 String genkeyText = exporter.toGenkeyText();

      public void setTrajectory(double[] xMetre, double[] yMetre, double[] diameterMetre)
      Set the well's own trajectory: per-node coordinates and per-segment diameter.

    • setWall

      public void setWall(double thickness, String thicknessUnit, String materialLabel, double conductivity, double heatCapacity, double density)
      Set the tubing wall's own thickness and a real material definition -- real, well-specific completion data. A real OLGA rule-check confirmed WALL (referencing a MATERIAL) is a required keyword for every PIPE in this exporter's own installed OLGA version, so this class cannot validly omit it. There is no default for any of the five parameters: an earlier version of this method accepted only a bare material LABEL (e.g. "STEEL") with no conductivity/capacity/density, which rule-checked as invalid ("MATERIAL with LABEL or NUMBER STEEL ... is not found") because OLGA has no built-in material by that name -- a real MATERIAL keyword with real properties must be declared, not assumed to already exist.
      Parameters:
      thickness - wall thickness, must be positive and finite
      thicknessUnit - "m" or "mm"
      materialLabel - wall material label (e.g. "STEEL"), must not be null or blank
      conductivity - thermal conductivity in W/m-C, must be positive and finite
      heatCapacity - specific heat capacity in J/kg-C, must be positive and finite
      density - density in kg/m3, must be positive and finite
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the thickness/conductivity/heatCapacity/density are not positive/finite, the thickness unit is not recognised, or the material label is null/blank

    • setHeatTransfer

      public void setHeatTransfer(double overallCoefficient, String overallCoefficientUnit, double ambientTemperature, String ambientTemperatureUnit)
      Set the flowpath's own overall (lumped) heat-transfer coefficient and ambient temperature -- real, well- and environment-specific data. There is no default: a real OLGA rule-check confirmed HEATTRANSFER is a required keyword for a FLOWPATH, so this class cannot validly omit it, but it will not fabricate a value either -- the caller must supply a real overall coefficient and ambient temperature (e.g. from the same completion/environment data used elsewhere in the study).
      Parameters:
      overallCoefficient - overall heat-transfer coefficient, must be positive and finite
      overallCoefficientUnit - "W/m2-C" or "W/m2-K" (numerically identical: both are per unit temperature DIFFERENCE, so a degree Celsius and a kelvin differ by the same amount)
      ambientTemperature - ambient temperature, must be finite
      ambientTemperatureUnit - "C" or "K"
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the coefficient is not positive/finite, the ambient temperature is not finite, or either unit is not recognised

    • setPvtFluidLabel

      public void setPvtFluidLabel(String label)
      Set the FLUID= label referenced by this flowpath's BRANCH statement -- the label a PVT table generator (e.g. OLGApropertyTableGenerator) already produced. Optional: when never called, toGenkeyText() emits a clearly marked TODO comment instead of a fabricated fluid reference, because a genkey flowpath is not valid OLGA input without a real one.
      Parameters:

    • formatNumber

      private static String formatNumber(double value)
      Format a single number with fixed-point precision, independent of the JVM's default locale -- a comma-decimal locale would otherwise silently corrupt every numeric value this class writes.

      Uses 8 decimal places uniformly, not the 4 an earlier version of this method used: pipe roughness is routinely 1e-5 to 1e-4 m, and 4 decimal places silently rounded every realistic roughness value straight to 0.0000 -- a genuinely destructive, silent precision loss caught by this class's own rule-check validation, not by code review. 8 decimal places safely represents every quantity this class emits (pressures, rates, coordinates, diameters, and roughness alike) without magnitude-dependent branching.

      Parameters:
      value - the value to format
      Returns:
      the formatted value
